name: Holder Construction
founded: 1960 (Robert M. Holder Jr., Georgia Tech civil engineer, Atlanta)
employees: ~2,000 (Forbes profile, accessed 2026; company publishes no count)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Holder is the quiet giant of hyperscale data-center construction — a private, family-owned Atlanta CM/design-builder that BD+C ranked the #1 US data-center contractor in its 2023 and 2024 reports (#2 in 2025, behind HITT), with trade analysis crediting it with more hyperscale square footage built than any other North American GC. Revenue roughly doubled in two years on the AI boom: $5.0B (2023, ENR #30) → $7.7B (2024, ENR #15) → a reported $10.2B (2025, reported ENR #12). CEO Beth Lowry says 60-70% of current projects are data centers; confirmed hyperscale work skews to Google (the ~$2B Fort Wayne IN campus; the New Albany OH 'Mustang Project') plus the $1.9B, ≥450 MW EdgeCore Mesa AZ campus and legacy Meta/Apple credits (Holder finished Apple Park). The company is strikingly low-publicity — no leadership page, no press room, no disclosed backlog — consistent with an NDA-heavy hyperscaler client base, which cuts both ways: its absence from the publicly named GC lineups of the newest 2025-26 mega-campuses (Stargate sites, Meta Hyperion/Prometheus) could be undisclosed private awards or share loss to Turner/DPR/Mortenson/HITT; public sources cannot distinguish. Collection gaps: no financial statements, no ownership statement (Forbes classifies it family-owned at #65 with $8.5B; aggregator ESOP claims are unverified and treated as unreliable), and the 2025 ENR figure comes from a secondary aggregator against a paywalled original.
ecosystemRole: The low-profile incumbent of hyperscale data-center general contracting: a repeat-relationship (>90%) CM/design-builder that has quietly delivered more hyperscale square footage than any named peer, anchoring Google's and EdgeCore's build programs while avoiding nearly all public visibility.

productsAndServices.name: Data & Telecom / Mission-Critical Construction
productsAndServices.description: The core franchise: hyperscale and enterprise data-center CM and design-build. Company-claimed portfolio: 610+ data & telecom projects, $76B volume, 12.9 GW delivered (the same page also cites '6.4 GW+ across the US' — treat the 6.4 GW US figure as the conservative read). Self-positions as 'the nation's largest data center builder' for the last 15 years, now building 'next-generation infrastructure to support AI workloads.'
highlights: Google: GC on the ~$2B, 700+ acre Fort Wayne, IN data center (broke ground April 2024) and Google's 'Mustang Project' in New Albany, OH — where Holder signed a formal OSHA Strategic Partnership with union trades
EdgeCore Mesa, AZ: $1.9B contract for a 3.1M sq ft, ≥450 MW critical-load, water-neutral air-cooled campus — Holder's largest publicly reported single award
Meta legacy: reported completed Facebook data centers in Fort Worth TX, New Albany OH, and Huntsville AL
Apple: replaced the Skanska/DPR JV mid-construction on Apple Park; Apple named among key clients in the chairman's Georgia Power board bio
Independent estimate: $3-4B/yr of data-center revenue — the highest estimate among Tier-1 DC contractors (vs Turner $1.5-2B, DPR $2-3B per the same analysis)
productsAndServices.positioning: BD+C #1 data-center contractor 2023 and 2024, #2 in 2025 behind HITT; 'when a hyperscaler needs a 100 MW campus built in 18 months, Holder is typically on the short list' (trade analysis). Differentiators cited by third parties: deep mission-critical PM/superintendent bench, MEP coordination with embedded commissioning, and a >90% repeat-client model.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Privately negotiated, largely unannounced repeat-relationship contracts with hyperscalers and data-center developers
productsAndServices.roadmap: EdgeCore Mesa buildout; Google program continuation; public sources cannot see the NDA'd pipeline — the central collection gap

productsAndServices.name: Aviation & Transportation
productsAndServices.description: National airport practice — 66 projects, $13.8B volume, 20 airports (company claims) — running some of the largest live US airport jobs: CM-at-risk lead of the $1.4B ATL Concourse D modernization (Holder / C.D. Moody / Bryson / Sovereign JV), the $950M Omaha Eppley Airfield terminal expansion (completion 2028), and the ~$1.8B Salt Lake City International redevelopment (Big-D/Holder JV).
highlights: ATL Concourse D: aviation-first modular strategy — 19 prefab modules built off-site and transported across the airfield, widening the concourse from 60 to ~100 ft; passed halfway with completion set for 2029
Omaha Eppley: terminal growing 375,000 → 646,000 sq ft
Home-market franchise at the world's busiest airport (Hartsfield-Jackson)
productsAndServices.positioning: Top-tier airport CM in JV-heavy public work — the diversification ballast against data-center cyclicality
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Public CM-at-risk awards, typically in JVs with MBE partners

productsAndServices.name: Corporate, Higher-Ed & Public Assembly
productsAndServices.description: The legacy diversified book: corporate campuses and offices, higher education, hospitality, interiors/adaptive reuse, and science & technology. Marquee credits include Apple Park (completion GC) and Mercedes-Benz Stadium (HHRM JV with Hunt, H.J. Russell, C.D. Moody). Client roster per the chairman's board bio: Apple, Google, Meta, State Farm, Atlanta Falcons, Ohio State, Norfolk Southern, Delta, Clemson, Cox Enterprises.
highlights: Clemson Core Campus via a Holder JV; Ohio State and other flagship-university work
>90% of work from repeat clients (company claim) across the whole book
productsAndServices.positioning: Blue-chip repeat-client roster concentrated in the Southeast, with Atlanta civic depth (Georgia Tech, Georgia Power board seats across two generations of leadership)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Steady-state; data centers absorb the growth capital

productsAndServices.name: Delivery Platform: Self-Perform, VDC & Prefabrication
productsAndServices.description: Services span construction management, design-build, self-perform trades, planning/design support, VDC/BIM coordination, preconstruction, prefabrication, quality, MEP/building technology, and sustainability. The self-perform list is telling: structural concrete, rough carpentry, hot-aisle containment, modular wall systems, site maintenance, and site safety systems — hot-aisle containment as an in-house trade is a data-center-specific capability.
highlights: Self-performed hot-aisle containment and modular wall systems — direct control of the data-hall fit-out critical path
Modular/prefab capability proven at airport scale (ATL Concourse D modules) and listed as a core service

OSHA Strategic Partnership on the Google Mustang site: TCIR target 10% below the BLS construction baseline, site-wide 6-ft fall protection, OSHA-30 supervisors, daily audits — with IBEW, Pipefitters, Operating Engineers, Carpenters, and Laborers as signatories
productsAndServices.positioning: Capability depth without publicity — no trade-press tech features exist because the firm doesn't court them; the OSHA partnership document is the rare primary artifact of how it actually runs sites

recentDevelopments.headline: EdgeCore selects Holder for its $1.9B Mesa, AZ hyperscale campus — 3.1M sq ft, ≥450 MW critical load, water-neutral air-cooled design
recentDevelopments.read: Largest publicly reported single award in company history, and evidence the franchise extends beyond Google to the developer/colocation tier.

strategyRead: 1. (High confidence) We assess Holder operates the most deliberately low-visibility franchise among top-tier data-center GCs — no leadership page, no press room, no disclosed backlog — as a commercial strategy matched to NDA-heavy hyperscaler clients, not as weakness. The cost is analytical: its market share can only be tracked through client-side disclosures and rankings surveys, both of which lag and undercount unannounced work.

2. (High confidence) We assess concentration risk is comparable to HITT's but less visible: the CEO's own 60-70%-of-projects figure plus a confirmed client set skewing to Google and EdgeCore means an AI-capex slowdown — or a single Google program pause — is the dominant earnings risk, against an undisclosed balance sheet.

3. (Moderate confidence) We assess Holder has ceded relative public share in the newest mega-campus wave: the 2025-26 record awards (Meta Hyperion/Louisiana, Stargate sites, Meta Indiana, Microsoft Wisconsin) are publicly held by Turner, DPR, Mortenson, HITT, Fortis, and Hensel Phelps, with no reported Holder role. The alternative explanation — undisclosed private awards consistent with its NDA model — cannot be excluded, and Holder's reported 2025 revenue (~$10.2B) kept growing regardless.

4. (Moderate confidence) We assess the Georgia Power board seats held consecutively by both the chairman and now CEO Lowry are strategically material, not ceremonial: in the current cycle, power availability is the gating input for data-center siting in Holder's home Southeast market, and utility-level relationships are exactly the collection channel a power-constrained builder wants.

5. (Moderate confidence) We assess the aviation practice (ATL Concourse D $1.4B, Omaha $950M, SLC ~$1.8B) as deliberate counter-cyclical ballast — long-duration public work with JV structures that keeps the bench utilized independent of hyperscale capex timing.

6. (Low confidence) We assess total 2025 revenue at ~$10.2B and ENR 2026 rank at #12 based on a single secondary aggregator against a paywalled ENR original; Forbes' $8.5B (2026 list) suggests the true figure depends heavily on fiscal-cutoff definitions. Treat the precision as indicative.

decisionMakers.name: Beth A. Lowry
decisionMakers.title: President & Chief Executive Officer
background: First woman to hold the role in company history; CEO following Tommy Holder's December 2021 step-down (exact assumption date not publicly stated)
Joined Holder as an intern in 1994 and full-time in 1995 after the University of Florida's Rinker School (building construction); Rinker Hall of Fame; elected to the National Academy of Construction
Elected to Georgia Power's board of directors May 2026; boards include Kennesaw State University Foundation, Atlanta Police Foundation, AGC Georgia
On the book under her leadership: 60-70% of current projects are data centers, ~$10B of projects planned for the fiscal year (September 2025)

decisionMakers.name: Thomas M. 'Tommy' Holder
decisionMakers.title: Chairman (former President & CEO, 1989-2021)
background: Son of founder Robert M. Holder Jr.; joined 1976 in preconstruction; President & CEO 1989, Chairman 1997; stepped down as CEO December 2021, remains Chairman
Grew revenue from $250M (1989) to $8B+; Georgia Tech graduate; Georgia Power board; Board Chair of the Georgia Tech Foundation and Children's Healthcare of Atlanta
2025 Four Pillar Award honoree (metro-Atlanta civic honor)
